reason:
The PROBLEM is real and I reproduced it exactly; the FIX is wrong against the real source, so this is REFUTED with the corrected fix below. Reproduction (Playwright, chromium, 1440x960, ?v=light&state=full): .strip is 1034px wide. Ticks measure at 1.86 / 34.69 / 66.79 / 98.89 per cent of the strip regardless of data, because line 313 is `.strip-scale { position: absolute; left:0; right:0; bottom:0; display:flex; justify-content: space-between }` and line 634 emits marks from the hardcoded `[0,15,30,45].filter(n => n <= D.axisMax)`, while every dot (line 620) and the fortnight rule (line 631) are placed at `value / D.axisMax * 100`. Shipped oldest is 41 (fixture.js), so `D.axisMax = Math.max(45, Math.ceil((41+4)/5)*5) = 45` and the two systems coincide to within 14px at the 15d mark. Forcing the oldest job to 46 via addInitScript: axisMax becomes 50, every dot rescales (the 46-day dot moves to 92 per cent), the ticks do not move at all, and the 45d label sits at 1022.5px where 45 days truly falls at 930.6px - a 92px lie, close to the seat's claimed 100px. So the mechanism, the arithmetic and the class are all correct, and neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs asserts anything about tick placement.

What kills the fix: it opens with 'give .strip-scale position: relative'. .strip-scale is ALREADY position: absolute, and that is what pins it to `bottom: 0` of the 92px .strip. Setting it to relative drops it into flow inside a .strip whose only other children (.strip-axis, .fortnight, every .dot) are absolute, so the whole scale jumps from the bottom of the strip to y=0 and lands on top of the dots and the 'A fortnight' label. Second, absolutely positioning the tick children collapses .strip-scale to zero height, so ticks anchored `top: 0` render below the strip box and into the card padding unless the anchor is flipped to `bottom: 0` or an explicit height is restored. Third, `translateX(-50%)` at 0 and 100 per cent hangs half of 'today' and half of '45d' outside the strip; the fix says 'clamp the first and last' but names no mechanism, and the current space-between IS the edge-inset convention it would be discarding. Fourth, and the fix misses this entirely: it repositions the marks but leaves the mark SET hardcoded, so at axisMax 50 the correct fix puts 45d at 90 per cent and then the last tenth of the axis - the region where the oldest, most alarming job sits - carries no label at all. Positioning by value without deriving the marks from axisMax trades one wrong axis for a truncated one.

Severity: 'defect' is the right class and I would not raise it. On the frozen artifact under review every state renders axisMax 45, so nothing on screen is currently untrue - the worst live error is a 19-day dot reading as 18.5 days. It is a latent defect in code whose own comment ('the axis maximum is derived, never typed... a sixty-day job must not fall off the end of its own chart') promises the very generality the scale breaks, which is why it is worth fixing, but it is not 'misleading' today.
sharpenedFix: Two changes, both in the strip. (1) Derive the mark set from the axis instead of hardcoding it: build marks by stepping 15 from 0 while below axisMax and always append axisMax itself, dropping the penultimate mark if it lands within ~8 per cent of the end so the last two labels cannot collide - this guarantees the right-hand end of the axis is always named. (2) Keep `.strip-scale { position: absolute; left:0; right:0; bottom:0 }` exactly as it is, drop `display:flex; justify-content: space-between`, and give it an explicit `height: <the label line-height>` so it does not collapse. Render each mark as `position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: calc(var(--x) * 1%)` with `--x` set to `n / D.axisMax * 100`, the same expression the dots and the fortnight rule already use. For the horizontal anchor do NOT apply a blanket `translateX(-50%)`: give the first mark `transform: none` (left-aligned, as today), the last mark `transform: translateX(-100%)` (right-aligned), and `translateX(-50%)` to every mark between. That reproduces the edge-inset the current space-between gives for free, keeps both end labels inside the strip without a clamp hack, and makes each interior label's centre land on its true value. Re-run both gates afterwards - the scale is a `.t-unit` and moving it changes what backdrop it composites against.
breaks: Re-measure after it lands: (a) audit.mjs WCAG AA contrast for the .t-unit ticks - they move over the dot row and could sit under a dot's disc where the composited backdrop changes; (b) tick-to-tick collision at 390x844, where the strip is roughly a third of its 1034px desktop width and value-spaced labels bunch wherever axisMax is small - check the 0/15 pair specifically, since 'today' is 38.4px wide against 23px for the numeric marks; (c) the last mark against the right edge of .ages padding once it is right-aligned; (d) the 'A fortnight' rule's own label, which is offset `left: var(--gap-tight)` from a line at the same computed percentage as a possible tick and can now overlap one; (e) the .strip 92px height and the bottom:26px axis line, since collapsing .strip-scale to explicit height changes what sits in the bottom 26px; (f) the screen-reader paragraph on line 636 is unaffected and must stay the fallback of record.
